title: The New Jerusalem
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: The New Jerusalem is the holy city and final dwelling place of God with His redeemed people. It pictures the perfected people of God living forever in His presence, glory, purity, security, and joy.
summary: The New Jerusalem is the holy city and final dwelling place of God with His redeemed people. It pictures the perfected people of God living forever in His presence, glory, purity, security, and joy.
christFocus: Jesus Christ prepares and brings His people into the city of God. The Lamb is central to the New Jerusalem, and His redeemed people worship, serve, and reign in His light forever.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
The New Jerusalem is described as the holy city coming down from God. It is both city and bride imagery, showing the beauty, purity, and glory of God’s redeemed people dwelling with Him.

At the center of this hope is the presence of God. The greatest blessing of the city is not gold streets or beauty alone, but that God Himself dwells with His people.

The city is secure, holy, and full of light. Nothing unclean enters, and the Lamb is its lamp. The curse is gone, and God’s servants see His face.

This doctrine teaches that God’s saving purpose ends in communion. The story of Scripture moves toward God dwelling with His people in holiness and joy forever.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Many people long for home, safety, belonging, and beauty. The New Jerusalem answers that longing with something deeper than nostalgia: eternal dwelling with God.

This doctrine is precious for those who feel displaced, rejected, unsafe, or rootless. Christ is bringing His people into a city whose builder and maker is God.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Let the hope of the New Jerusalem shape your longing for home. Do not seek final security in earthly cities, houses, or acceptance. Live as a pilgrim whose future is with God, and pursue holiness as one destined for His holy city.
